newsitem.title: UK: Crucial UK by-election called for February 27.
newsitem.headline: Crucial UK by-election called for February 27.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservatives fired the starting gun on Monday for a crucial parliamentary by-election in the north-west England constituency of Wirral South, moving the writ for it in parliament.
Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell said earlier that polling would take place on February 27.
The by-election will be a key barometer of public opinion in the run-up to a general election which is expected to be held on or before May 1.
If the Conservatives lose the seat, which their candidate Barry Porter won at the 1992 general election with a majority of 8,183 votes, they will again be in a minority position in parliament.
A recent opinion poll in the constituency made the opposition Labour Party odds-on to gain the seat, putting it 16 percentage points ahead of the Conservatives.
Porter died on November 3. By convention, the party holding the seat of a member who dies or resigns must move a motion in parliament for a new poll within three months.
